title: Singaporeans and service in the Israel Defense Forces
asked: MPs asked whether the Ministry has substantiated information that Singaporeans served in the Israel Defense Forces in 2025, whether this breaches Singapore law and what action follows, and how the Government monitors and advises citizens against foreign military involvement. They also asked whether claims about two Singaporeans would be investigated, whether section 125 of the Penal Code or citizenship deprivation applies, and how policies are reviewed.
asked_by: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong, Mr Fadli Fawzi and Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
response: Mr K Shanmugam said MHA is aware of a foreign news report that two Singaporeans fought for the IDF in Gaza, but has no substantiated information confirming any Singaporean has served or is serving in the IDF. He said Singaporeans should not participate in foreign armed conflicts not involving Singapore, and those found fighting or planning to fight will be dealt with under laws including the Internal Security Act, with multiple citizens possibly deprived of Singapore citizenship. He said the Government has asked the Israeli government and received no response, and that if credible information emerges, action will be taken regardless of which foreign force is involved.

key_points.point: MHA is aware of a foreign news report that two Singaporeans fought for the IDF in Gaza.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is aware of a foreign news report stating that two Singaporeans were among those who fought for the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) during the conflict in Gaza.

key_points.point: MHA has no substantiated information confirming any Singaporean has served or is serving in the IDF.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: The Ministry has no substantiated information confirming that any Singaporean has served, or is serving, in the IDF.

key_points.point: Singaporeans should not participate in any foreign armed conflict not involving Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: Singaporeans should not participate in any foreign armed conflict not involving Singapore.

key_points.point: Those found fighting or planning to fight in foreign armed conflicts will be dealt with sternly under Singapore laws.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: If Singaporeans are found to be fighting or even planning to fight in foreign armed conflicts, these persons will be dealt with sternly in accordance with our laws.

key_points.point: They can be dealt with under the Internal Security Act if found to be a threat to national security.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: And they can be dealt with under the Internal Security Act if they are found to be a threat to our national security.

key_points.point: Those holding multiple citizenships may be deprived of Singapore citizenship.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: Those found holding multiple citizenships may also be deprived of their Singapore citizenship.

key_points.point: The Government has asked the Israeli government and has not received a response.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: The Government has asked the Israeli government. We have not received a response.

key_points.point: Whether section 125 applies depends on the facts and would require investigation.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: whether section 125 applies really depends on the facts and that would require investigation.

key_points.point: The current legal framework, including the Internal Security Act, is adequate.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: the current legal framework, including the Internal Security Act, is adequate.

key_points.point: Action will be taken regardless of which foreign force is involved.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: It does not matter to us whether you are fighting for Israel or Ukraine or Russia or some other Middle Eastern country or a terrorist organisation.

left_open: Whether serving in the IDF specifically breaches section 125 of the Penal Code 1871.
Whether identified individuals would be prosecuted under section 125 or another named law.
How nationality obligations with the other state are handled.
What upstream measures are being considered to tighten guidelines.
Whether policies will be reviewed to mitigate risks of unauthorised foreign military involvement.
supplementary: Clarifying legal basis, foreign engagement and upstream measures for Singaporeans in foreign militaries.
